Exactly two attempts exist. Attempt 1 is fully archived under artifacts/attempt1/; it failed the frozen Part A counter-path criterion (repair=0) due to an implementation defect in the staleness injection (substrate key prefix), which was fixed to mirror the parent packet's bump call. No run was discarded; attempt 2 is the reporting attempt. Neither attempt was re-run to chase the null control.

Verdict MIXED; no silent preference was applied. The cross-attempt sign instability and the fact that latency_ms is measured (not formula-derived) argue against deterministic counter-formula coupling, but the literal observed-data gate failure stands as recorded.

Controls are not part of spec.decision_rule.overall; the frozen table PASS/PASS/PASS -> COMPLETE/SUPPORTS was applied exactly. A downstream AUDIT/DIRECTOR may weight the MIXED NC differently; the raw per-stratum values for both attempts are preserved for recomputation.

f*_latency_ms is NOT IDENTIFIABLE on this single-node localhost substrate: the serving denominator (cold - inherited mean latency) CI spans zero in both attempts ([-0.719,1.005] ms and [-1.234,0.200] ms around means of ~24.8 ms). The primary unit is therefore bytes, where the denominator is robustly positive (CI [894.63, 1013.17]). Any ms- or time-based amortization claim must be re-measured on a WAN-like substrate with non-negligible transfer time.

f*_bytes is substrate- and content-bound: 971.1 bytes cold payload vs 16.7 bytes inherited payload per trajectory on these fixtures (304 revalidation on localhost). It measures protocol-level payload saving, not wall-clock or money saving.
payload_bytes is an auxiliary non-counter measurement (not one of the eight frozen integer counters); it is reset per trajectory like the counters but excluded from the eight-counter criteria.

This affects only latency cross-arm interpretation, not the eight-counter gates, the CIs' payload/requests results, or f*.
Build/verify/serving costs are measured wall-clock (ms) and payload bytes from the dry run; no token, model-call or dollar quantities exist anywhere in the computation, by construction.
